tool.name: repertoire_profiler
tool.description: Ig/TR repertoire: V(D)J annotation, clonal groups, mutation load, alignments and trees
tool.command:
#import re #set $pipeline = $__tool_directory__ + '/..' set -o pipefail &&
## apptainer runs the processes of the pipeline (requirement of the tool, or module loaded by the job configuration of the server) command -v apptainer > /dev/null || { echo 'ERROR: apptainer not found in the PATH of the Galaxy job' >&2; exit 1; } &&
## nextflow.config uses ./bin/... paths, relative to the launch folder (the job working folder) ln -s '$pipeline/bin' bin &&
## sequences (sample_path) and metadata (meta_path): copied in the job folder, which is mounted in the containers #if $input.input_type == 'zip': cp '$input.fasta_zip' sample.zip && #set $sample = 'sample.zip' #elif $input.input_type == 'folder': ## folder of fasta files with a single sequence each (list collection or several datasets): rebuilt in the job folder, ## one file per dataset, named after its collection element identifier (or its dataset name), without its fasta extension, ## with only letters, digits, _ and - (the file names are not quoted in the processes of the pipeline), at most 100 characters, ## made unique, plus the .fasta extension. The sequence names are the fasta headers, not the file names. mkdir sample && #set $file_names = [] #for $fasta in $input.fasta_folder: #set $name = str($fasta.element_identifier) #set $parts = $name.rsplit('.', 1) #if len($parts) == 2 and $parts[1].lower() in ['fasta', 'fa', 'fas', 'fna', 'txt', 'seq', 'faa']: #set $name = $parts[0] #end if #set $name = re.sub('^-', '_', re.sub('[^A-Za-z0-9_-]', '_', $name))[:100] or 'sequence' #set $file_name = $name #set $i = 1 #while $file_name in $file_names: #set $i = $i + 1 #set $file_name = $name + '_' + str($i) #end while #silent $file_names.append($file_name) cp '$fasta' 'sample/${file_name}.fasta' && #end for #set $sample = 'sample' #else: ## one or several fasta files, with one or several sequences each: merged into a single file, split by the Split_fasta process awk 'NF' #for $fasta in $input.fasta# '$fasta'#end for# > sample.fasta && #set $sample = 'sample.fasta' #end if #if $metadata.add_metadata == 'yes': cp '$metadata.meta_file' metadata.tsv && #end if
## nextflow.config of the job (copied by the pipeline into the reports folder): values of the form, then of the optional parameter file, then those of the server python3 '$__tool_directory__/fill_config.py' --template '$pipeline/nextflow.config' --locked '$__tool_directory__/locked_params.txt' --galaxy-inputs '$form_values' --galaxy-ignore input_type,add_metadata,tables,zip ## IgBlast chains: one TRUE/FALSE parameter per chain in nextflow.config, a multiple select in the form --galaxy-flags chains=igblast_B_heavy_chain,igblast_B_lambda_chain,igblast_B_kappa_chain,igblast_T_alpha_chain,igblast_T_beta_chain,igblast_T_gamma_chain,igblast_T_delta_chain #if $advanced.params: --values '$advanced.params' #end if --set "sample_path=\$PWD/$sample" #if $metadata.add_metadata == 'yes': --set "meta_path=\$PWD/metadata.tsv" #else: --set meta_path=NULL #end if --set system_exec=local --set "apptainer_local_images=\${RP_APPTAINER_CACHE:?the RP_APPTAINER_CACHE variable must be set by the Galaxy administrators (folder of the apptainer images)}" --set "cluster_runOptions=\${RP_APPTAINER_OPTIONS:---no-home --bind /pasteur} --env XDG_CACHE_HOME=/tmp" --set "phylo_tree_model_path=$pipeline/bin/AB_model" --set phylo_tree_itol_subscription=FALSE --set "out_path_ini=\$PWD/results" --set result_folder_name=repertoire_profiler --cpus "\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1}" --memory-mb "\${GALAXY_MEMORY_MB:-}" -o nextflow.config &&
export NXF_HOME="\$PWD/.nextflow_home" && export NXF_OFFLINE=true && export APPTAINER_TMPDIR="\${APPTAINER_TMPDIR:-\$PWD/apptainer_tmp}" && mkdir -p "\$APPTAINER_TMPDIR" && nextflow -C nextflow.config run '$pipeline/main.nf' -work-dir work -ansi-log false &&
## outputs: the HTML report carries the whole result folder (its links work in Galaxy, its download is a zip of the folder) results_dir=\$(ls -d results/repertoire_profiler_*) && cp "\$results_dir/report.html" '$report' && mkdir -p '$report.extra_files_path' && cp -r "\$results_dir"/. '$report.extra_files_path' && #if $output_options.zip: (cd results && python3 -m zipfile -c '$results_zip' "\$(basename "\$results_dir")") && #end if #if $output_options.tables: mkdir tables && cp "\$results_dir"/tsv/*.tsv tables/ && #end if echo "result folder: \$results_dir"

param.name: input_type
param.label: Sequences (sample_path)
param.help:
Usage notice: https://github.com/gael-millot/repertoire_profiler/tree/web
Nucleotide sequences to analyze. They do not have to be Ig or TR sequences: the pipeline filters them.

param.name: fasta
param.label: Fasta file(s)
param.help: One or several fasta files (or a collection), each with one or several sequences. They are merged into a single fasta file. Only the first 100 characters of the headers are used as sequence names, and the non alphanumeric characters are replaced by underscores.

param.name: fasta_folder
param.label: Fasta files of the folder
param.help: Fasta files containing a single sequence each, given to the pipeline as a folder (sample_path): a list collection, or several fasta datasets of the history. Galaxy cannot upload a folder as such: in the Upload window, Collection tab, select all the files of the folder to get them as a list collection. Only the first 100 characters of the headers are used as sequence names, and the non alphanumeric characters are replaced by underscores.

param.name: fasta_zip
param.label: Zip archive
param.help: Zip of a single fasta file with several sequences, or of fasta files with one sequence each (extensions fasta, fa, fas, fna, txt, seq or faa).

param.name: add_metadata
param.label: Metadata (meta_path)
param.help: Optional table adding information to the results: replacement of the sequence names, shape of the tree leaves.

param.name: meta_file
param.label: Metadata table
param.help: Tab-separated table with a header line, including a column of sequence names. At least one sequence of the fasta files must be in this table, but not all of them.

param.name: meta_seq_names
param.label: Column of the sequence names (meta_seq_names)
param.help: Column of the metadata table with the sequence names, i.e., the headers of the fasta sequences without the starting >. Only the first 100 characters of the headers are used and the non alphanumeric characters are replaced by underscores.

validator.message: A column name of the metadata table is expected

param.name: meta_name_replacement
param.label: Column of the replacement names (meta_name_replacement)
param.help: Column of the metadata table with names replacing the sequence names in the returned tables and figures (the initial name stays in the initial_sequence_id column), also used to tag the donut slices. Empty values and NA are not considered. NULL if not required (meta_name_replacement and meta_legend cannot be both NULL).

validator.message: A column name of the metadata table or NULL is expected

param.name: meta_legend
param.label: Column for the tree leaves (meta_legend)
param.help: Graphics section of nextflow.config. Column of the metadata table used to shape the tree leaves (trees only), e.g., KD or names: leaf size if numeric (germ_tree_leaf_size is then ignored), leaf color by class otherwise (germ_tree_leaf_shape is then ignored). Empty values and NA are not considered. NULL if not required.

validator.message: A column name of the metadata table or NULL is expected

section.name: annotation
section.title: Ig annotation
section.help: Most probable V, D, J and C alleles of each sequence, with AssignGenes.py igblast of Change-O.

param.name: igblast_organism
param.label: Organism (igblast_organism)
param.help: Option --organism of AssignGenes.py igblast. The pipeline currently supports human and mouse only.

param.name: igblast_loci
param.label: Receptor (igblast_loci)
param.help: Option --loci of AssignGenes.py igblast.

param.name: chains
param.label: IMGT databases searched by IgBlast
param.help: Warning: select several chains only if the clonal groups do not matter for you, since the clonal distance might not be adapted to a mix of chains.

param.name: chains
param.label: IMGT databases searched by IgBlast
param.help: Warning: select several chains only if the clonal groups do not matter for you, since the clonal distance might not be adapted to a mix of chains.

section.name: clones
section.title: Clonal groups (clustering) and mutation load
section.help: Clonal groups: shazam::distToNearest() and DefineClones.py of Change-O (clone_id column of clone_assigned_seq.tsv). Germline sequence of each clonal group: CreateGermlines.py of Change-O. Mutation load: shazam::observedMutations().

param.name: clone_strategy
param.label: Ambiguous gene assignments (clone_strategy)
param.help: Option --act of DefineClones.py. first: only the first gene is used when a sequence is assigned to several genes (e.g., IGHV4-30-4*09 for IGHV4-30-4*09,IGHV4-31*03), to restrict the clonal groups to the most confident assignment. set: clonal groups made of the sequences sharing at least one gene, directly or indirectly, for a broader grouping.

param.name: clone_model
param.label: Distance model (clone_model)
param.help: Option --model of DefineClones.py: distance between sequences used to cluster them. ham: nucleotide Hamming distance, aa: amino acid Hamming distance. See https://shazam.readthedocs.io/en/stable/topics/distToNearest/#details

param.name: clone_normalize
param.label: Distance normalization (clone_normalize)
param.help: Option --norm of DefineClones.py.

param.name: clone_distance
param.label: Distance threshold (clone_distance)
param.help: Option --dist of DefineClones.py: distance (proportion) below which two sequences belong to the same clonal group. See https://shazam.readthedocs.io/en/stable/vignettes/DistToNearest-Vignette/

param.name: clone_germline_kind
param.label: Germline sequence of the clonal groups (clone_germline_kind)
param.help: Option -g of CreateGermlines.py. With full, the initial germline_alignment column is kept and the germline_alignment_full column is created.
param.option: dmask: germline with the D segment masked
vonly: germline of the V segment only

param.name: clone_mut_obs_seq
param.label: Observed sequences (clone_mut_obs_seq)
param.help: Column of clone_assigned_seq.tsv compared to the germline sequences (argument sequenceColumn of shazam::observedMutations()). Sequences with IMGT gaps (dots) are required.

validator.message: A column name of clone_assigned_seq.tsv is expected

param.name: clone_mut_germ_seq
param.label: Germline sequences (clone_mut_germ_seq)
param.help: Column of clone_assigned_seq.tsv used as germline sequences (argument germlineColumn of shazam::observedMutations()), depending on the germline sequence above: germline_alignment_d_mask for dmask, germline_alignment_v_region for vonly and germline_alignment_full for full. Sequences with IMGT gaps (dots) are required.

validator.message: A column name of clone_assigned_seq.tsv is expected

param.name: clone_mut_regionDefinition
param.label: Regions of the mutation counts (clone_mut_regionDefinition)
param.help: Regions and boundaries of the mutation counts and frequencies (argument regionDefinition of shazam::observedMutations()). NULL: the entire sequence. The region definitions require sequences aligned following the IMGT schema. See https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/shazam/html/IMGT_SCHEMES.html

section.name: alignments
section.title: Alignments
section.help: Nucleotide and amino acid alignments with Mafft or Abalign. Abalign aligns the variable region only, with the FWR and CDR regions as constraints.

param.name: align_clone_nb
param.label: Minimum number of sequences per clonal group (align_clone_nb)
param.help: Minimum number of non-identical sequences of a clonal group to align it.

param.name: align_soft
param.label: Aligner (align_soft)
param.help: Mafft is always used for the query, igblast_full, trimmed, c_sequence_alignment and c_germline_alignment sequences below. Mafft by default, as more alignment parameters can be set.

param.name: align_seq
param.label: Aligned sequences (align_seq)
param.help: Columns of productive_seq.tsv aligned, nucleotides and amino acids. Use sequence_alignment if you do not know what to use. See the definition of the columns at https://github.com/gael-millot/repertoire_profiler#output
param.option: query: sequence and query_sequence_aa (complete translation of the query, can have stop codons)
igblast_full: sequence and sequence_aa (translation after trimming, starting with the V region)

param.name: align_abalign_options
param.label: Abalign options (align_abalign_options)
param.help: See https://github.com/gael-millot/repertoire_profiler/blob/master/bin/abalign_CLI_help.txt. The -ah/-al and -sp options are already set by the pipeline.

param.name: align_mafft_all_options
param.label: Mafft options, alignment of all the sequences (align_mafft_all_options)
param.help: See https://mafft.cbrc.jp/alignment/software/manual/manual.html, notably the Speed-oriented methods section for thousands of sequences. Keep --thread -1 to use the available resources.

param.name: align_mafft_clonal_options
param.label: Mafft options, alignments of the clonal groups (align_mafft_clonal_options)
param.help: See https://mafft.cbrc.jp/alignment/software/manual/manual.html. Keep --thread -1 to use the available resources.

section.name: graphics
section.title: Graphics
section.help: Trees of the clonal groups and donuts of the clonal group frequencies. The meta_legend parameter of this section of nextflow.config is with the metadata table above.

param.name: germ_tree_kind
param.label: Tree layout (germ_tree_kind)
param.help: See https://yulab-smu.top/treedata-book/chapter4.html#tree-layouts

param.name: germ_tree_duplicate_seq
param.label: Keep the identical sequences in the trees (germ_tree_duplicate_seq)
param.help: No: identical sequences (from different cells or sequence names) are removed from the trees, which is useful when many identical sequences overload the trees. The removed sequences are indicated in the title of the tree plots.

param.name: germ_tree_leaf_color
param.label: Leaf color (germ_tree_leaf_color)
param.help: R color name or hexadecimal code (e.g., #FF0000), NULL for the default. Ignored if meta_legend is a non numeric column of the metadata table.

validator.message: NULL, an R color name or a hexadecimal color code is expected

param.name: germ_tree_leaf_shape
param.label: Leaf shape (germ_tree_leaf_shape)
param.help: R point shape (pch). See https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/graphics/html/points.html

param.name: germ_tree_leaf_size
param.label: Leaf size in mm (germ_tree_leaf_size)
param.help: The plot is 120 x 120 mm. Ignored if meta_legend is a numeric column of the metadata table.

param.name: germ_tree_label_size
param.label: Leaf label size in mm (germ_tree_label_size)
param.help: The plot is 120 x 120 mm.

param.name: germ_tree_label_hjust
param.label: Leaf label adjustment (germ_tree_label_hjust)
param.help: Decreasing negative values move the labels away from the leaves.

param.name: germ_tree_label_rigth
param.label: Labels on the right (germ_tree_label_rigth)
param.help: Only for the rectangular layout.

param.name: germ_tree_label_outside
param.label: Labels outside of the plot region (germ_tree_label_outside)
param.help: Useful if the labels are truncated.

param.name: germ_tree_right_margin
param.label: Right margin in inches (germ_tree_right_margin)
param.help: For a graphic device of 5 inches width.

param.name: donut_palette
param.label: Donut palette (donut_palette)
param.help: ColorBrewer palette of the donuts. See https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/scale_brewer.html#palettes

param.name: donut_hole_size
param.label: Donut hole size (donut_hole_size)
param.help: Proportion: 0 for a pie chart, 1 for a donut of null thickness.

param.name: donut_hole_text
param.label: Sum of the frequencies in the hole (donut_hole_text)

param.name: donut_hole_text_size
param.label: Font size of the hole text in mm (donut_hole_text_size)
param.help: Ignored if the sum of the frequencies is not displayed.

param.name: donut_border_color
param.label: Border color (donut_border_color)
param.help: R color name (e.g., black, white, gray50) or hexadecimal code.

validator.message: An R color name or a hexadecimal color code is expected

param.name: donut_border_size
param.label: Border size in mm (donut_border_size)
param.help: The plot is 120 x 120 mm.

param.name: donut_annotation_distance
param.label: Distance of the annotations (donut_annotation_distance)
param.help: Distance from the center of the slice: 0 at the center, 0.5 at the edge. Above 0.5, the donut is reduced to make room for the annotations. Ignored without metadata.

param.name: donut_annotation_size
param.label: Annotation font size in mm (donut_annotation_size)
param.help: Ignored without metadata.

param.name: donut_annotation_force
param.label: Repulsion between overlapping annotations (donut_annotation_force)
param.help: See ggrepel::geom_text_repel(). Ignored without metadata.

param.name: donut_annotation_force_pull
param.label: Attraction between an annotation and its slice (donut_annotation_force_pull)
param.help: See ggrepel::geom_text_repel(). Ignored without metadata.

param.name: donut_legend_width
param.label: Relative width of the legend (donut_legend_width)
param.help: Width of the legend sector, on the right of the plot, relative to the plot width: 1 splits the device in two halves, 0 leaves no room for the legend, which overlays the plot.

param.name: donut_legend_box_space
param.label: Space between the legend squares in mm (donut_legend_box_space)

param.name: donut_legend_limit
param.label: Classes in the legend (donut_legend_limit)
param.help: NULL: the ten biggest sectors. all: all the sectors. A proportion, e.g., 0.4: only the sectors above 40% of the donut (the ten biggest, with a warning, if none).

validator.message: NULL, all or a proportion between 0 and 1 is expected

section.name: output_options
section.title: Outputs
section.help: The report dataset always contains the whole result folder: its links work in Galaxy and its download button gives a zip of the folder.

param.name: tables
param.label: Result tables as a collection
param.help: The .tsv files of the tsv folder of the results (productive_seq.tsv, clone_assigned_seq.tsv...) as a list collection, to analyze them with other Galaxy tools.

param.name: zip
param.label: Result folder as a separate zip dataset
param.help: Same content as the download of the report.

param.name: params
param.label: Parameter file (optional)
param.help: JSON object {"parameter": "value"} of nextflow.config parameters, e.g., {"clone_distance": "0.2"}. Its values replace those of the form, to reuse a set of parameters. The input and output paths, the execution parameters (Local / Cluster execution section of nextflow.config) and the iTOL parameters cannot be set.

tool.help:
**Usage notice**: https://github.com/gael-millot/repertoire_profiler/tree/web
-----
**What it does**
Runs the repertoire_profiler_ Nextflow pipeline on nucleotide sequences of immunoglobulins (Ig, BCR) or T cell receptors (TR): V(D)J annotation with IgBlast, selection of the productive sequences, clonal groups, mutation load, gene and allele repertoires, alignments, phylogenetic trees of the clonal groups, donuts, and an HTML report.
The form recapitulates the nextflow.config file of the pipeline: same sections, one field per parameter, with the name of the parameter in parentheses, so that the documentation of the pipeline (README and nextflow.config) applies. The execution parameters (Local / Cluster execution section) are set by Galaxy, and the iTOL upload of the trees is disabled.
.. _repertoire_profiler: https://github.com/gael-millot/repertoire_profiler
-----
**Inputs**
- Sequences (sample_path): one or several fasta files, a folder of fasta files, or a zip archive of fasta files. Folder: Galaxy cannot upload a folder as such. Select all the files of the folder in the *Collection* tab of *Upload* (then *Start*, *Build* and *Create list*): they form a list collection, given to the pipeline as a folder. - Metadata (meta_path, optional): a tab-separated table with a column of sequence names (meta_seq_names), used to rename the sequences (meta_name_replacement) and to shape the tree leaves (meta_legend). - Parameter file (optional): a JSON object {"parameter": "value"} of nextflow.config parameters, which replaces the values of the form.
-----
**Outputs**
- *report and result folder*: the HTML report of the run. This dataset also contains the whole result folder of the pipeline (tsv, pdf, figures, alignments, phylo, repertoires and reports folders, see the Output section of the README), so that the links of the report work in Galaxy. **To save the result folder, click on the download button of this dataset: you get a zip of the folder.** - *tables* (optional): the .tsv files of the tsv folder, as a list collection, for further analyses in Galaxy. - *result folder (zip)* (optional): the result folder as a separate zip dataset.
The results stay in the history: they can also be exported to a storage configured in the Galaxy server (Export datasets).
-----
**Duration**
The whole pipeline runs inside a single Galaxy job. A run of a few dozens of sequences takes about 15 minutes, longer the first time on a server, which pulls the container images of the pipeline.
